title: Rationale for when invalid value default differs from missing value default
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

It seems for most properties, an invalid value default is the same as the missing value default, e.g. we do this for the following:
* [referrer policy](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#referrer-policy-attributes)
* [lazy loading](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#lazy-loading-attributes)
* [fetch priority](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-priority-attributes)
* [translate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-translate-attribute)
* [dir](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-dir-attribute)
* [decoding](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-img-decoding)
* [kind](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-track-kind)
* [shape](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-area-shape)
* [scope](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-th-scope)
* [autocomplete](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-form-autocomplete)
* [type](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-input-type)
* [wrap](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-textarea-wrap)
* [method](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-fs-method)
* [enctype](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-fs-enctype)
* [shadowrootmode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-template-shadowrootmode)
* [hidden](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-hidden-attribute)
* [contenteditable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#contenteditable)
* [spellcheck](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-spellcheck)
* [draggable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-draggable-attribute)
* [popovertargetaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-popovertargetaction)
* [behavior](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-marquee-behavior)
* [direction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-marquee-direction)

From a scan of the spec there are five exceptions:
* [CORS](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#cors-settings-attributes)
* [preload](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-media-preload) has both being implementation defined
* [writingmode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#writing-suggestions)
* [autocapitalize](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-autocapitalize)
* [popover](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-popover-none-state)

I'd be interested to understand the rationale for these cases where an invalid value is not treated the same as a missing value. In particular, [writingsuggestions](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10018) was added recently, I didn't see any discussion around the invalid value default choice, but this was pointed to as an example for why [handwriting should have an invalid value default of true](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/5750334/comment/22f11bf7_cd37c0a4/), but I don't understand the rationale for when we should have a different invalid value default from the missing value default.

This seems like we should be consistent unless there is a reason to deviate. In particular, writingsuggestions and handwriting seem very similar to spellcheck which does have the same invalid value and missing value defaults.

@sanketj @mfreed7
